transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, basically, I'm here because things got a bit out of control recently. 

I work in landscaping, and I went from just being a normal crew guy to... well, suddenly I was trying to run three different bids all at once. I was calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, and just messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. I just kept going and going, like I couldn't shut it off.
During this time, were you hearing voices or seeing things that other people couldn’t?

No, um, nothing like that. I wasn't hearing voices or seeing anything that wasn't there. It was really just... just my own thoughts, you know? Just me getting way too carried away with all those ideas. But no, no voices or anything.
During that time, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Um, no, not really. I think I was sleeping about the same as I usually do. I'd still crash at night and wake up for work the next day. I didn't really notice needing less sleep or skipping it or anything, if that's what you mean. Just... normal sleep, mostly.
Were you hospitalized because of this period?

No, um, I wasn't in the hospital. I didn't have to go or anything like that. I just... I just kind of burned myself out doing all those bids and talking to everyone, but no, I never got admitted anywhere.
During that period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

No, um, it didn't cause any serious problems. I still showed up to my landscaping job every day and got all the work done. My boss didn't complain or anything. And things with my family and friends were fine, too. It was really just me being super focused on all those extra projects, but it didn't ruin anything or get me in trouble.
During that time, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people probably couldn’t?

Yeah, I did. I honestly believed I was about to become the main guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. Like I was going to take over all of it. Even though, realistically, I’m still just trying to keep my regular small jobs paid up. But at the time, I just felt like I could easily take on a huge level of work like that and succeed.
During that time, were you much more irritable than usual?

Yeah, I was. Before I crashed, I just felt really fired up... almost bigger than myself, I guess. But because of that, if a coworker questioned my plan or told me I needed to slow down, I'd just snap at him. I reacted way harder than made sense for the situation. So yeah, I was definitely a lot more irritable if people pushed back on what I was doing.
About how many days did that unusually energized, overconfident period last?

It lasted about two weeks. That whole fired-up, overconfident stretch started right when I began remaking myself for this big park pitch I wanted to do. So yeah, it went on for about two weeks total, and then I just crashed.
During that two-week period, were you talking much more than usual or feeling like you couldn’t stop talking?

No, not really. I mean, I was definitely fired up, but I didn't feel like I couldn't stop talking or anything. I was probably actually more in my own head, just... thinking about all the plans I had. So, no, I don't think I was talking any more than I usually do.
During that two-week period, were you much more active than usual in starting or taking on projects?

Yeah, definitely. I was taking on a lot more than usual. I'd be up before daylight, just... loading tools, sketching out new planting beds, pricing out native plants. And even after working a full day outside, I still felt like I had to keep going. I was just constantly starting new things for that pitch I was working on.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, like I mentioned a minute ago, that whole fired-up stretch started when I was remaking myself for the park pitch, and it lasted about two weeks. But right after that, I just completely crashed. And when I crashed... yeah, that's when I felt really down all day and just lost interest in everything.
After that crash, did the depressed period last at least two weeks?

Yeah, it definitely lasted at least two weeks. Honestly, the depression has been hanging over me for about a year now, off and on. But this latest crash... it's just the worst it's gotten. It's been going on way longer than a couple of weeks.
